bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: The Simple Formula

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, converting to an annual figure helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For most full-time employees, a 38-hour week is the benchmark under the Fair Work system. This article explains the conversion, the role of the National Minimum Wage, casual loading, superannuation, and tax—all with a focus on the **minimum wage melbourne** context.

### The 38-Hour Week Assumption

When you use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, the annual estimate assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a standard full-time role, 38 hours per week is the typical starting point. If your hours differ, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. The formula then becomes: annual gross ≈ hourly × 38 × 52.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Multiply by 38 gives $1,004.90 per week, and by 52 gives $52,254.80 per year. This is the minimum annual gross for an adult employee not covered by an award or agreement. If you are looking at **minimum wage melbourne** rates, note that some awards or enterprise agreements may set higher minimums.

### Fortnightly Pay and the 52-Week Year

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the minimum wage example: $1,004.90 per week × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. This can be handy for budgeting if you receive pay every two weeks. The annual figure remains the same regardless of pay frequency.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week. However, most employees are covered by a modern award or registered agreement that may specify higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides more detail on the current rate and how it applies. If you are in a specific job, check the relevant pay guide or award—the national minimum is a floor, not a target.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate, as per the Fair Work Ombudsman. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). On the [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading**—always start with the base hourly rate. The tool will add the loading for you.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your wage. The estimate applies 12% to your annualised ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, on the minimum wage annual gross of $52,254.80, super would be an additional $6,270.58 per year. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more on how super interacts with salary packaging.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

The annual estimate applies the 2026–27 resident tax scale and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income from $18,201 to $45,000 is taxed at 15%, then 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of calculation. No HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging are deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For a detailed breakdown of take-home pay, visit [take-home pay](/topics/take-home).

### Average Earnings for Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352.40 per year. All employees total earnings (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for any specific job. If you are comparing a salary offer, remember that averages can be skewed by high earners. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context.

### Putting It All Together

To convert your hourly rate to annual pay:
1. Multiply your base hourly rate by your weekly hours (assume 38 if full-time).
2. Multiply that weekly figure by 52 to get annual gross.
3. Add 25% casual loading if applicable (check the box on the timesheet).
4. Super is 12% on top of ordinary earnings.
5. Tax and Medicare are estimated using the resident scale and 2% levy.

For **minimum wage melbourne** workers, the current national minimum gives $52,254.80 per year before tax and super. But many awards in Melbourne (such as hospitality, retail, or manufacturing) set higher rates. Always check your specific award or agreement via the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides. The [pay guides](/blog) page links to official resources.

Remember: this estimate assumes a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for comparison, not a binding calculation. Use the [reference tables](/data) for more detailed tax and super figures.
